summary: Concentrated: 98 holdings, but the top ten are 67% of the portfolio.
Trades moderately: about 31% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for at least 7.5 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are cheaper.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 2 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Founded in 1920 by Bill Tweedy, who shared an office building with Benjamin Graham. Warren Buffett used the firm as his broker in the 1950s and 1960s and bought his first Berkshire shares through it. Affiliated Managers Group bought 70% of the firm in 1997.
profile.approach: Classic Graham-style value: low price to book value and earnings, insider buying, sharp price falls, smaller companies.
known: Buffett wrote that the firm beat the Dow and S&P 500 by wide margins from 1966 to 1982.
profile.note: Much of Tweedy, Browne's money is in non-US shares, which the 13F does not include.
